# 2 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** It is also found in the records that Jeremiah the prophet ordered those who were being deported to take some of the fire, as has been told,

**2** and that the prophet, having given them the law, charged those who were being deported not to forget the commandments of the LORD, nor to be led astray in their minds when they saw the gold and silver idols and their adornment.

**3** And with other such words he exhorted them that the law should not depart from their hearts.

**4** It was also in the writing that the prophet, having received an oracle, ordered that the tent and the ark should follow with him, as he went out to the mountain where Moses had gone up and had seen the inheritance of God.

**5** And Jeremiah came and found a cave-dwelling, and he brought there the tent and the ark and the altar of incense, and he blocked up the entrance.

**6** And some of those who followed came up to mark the way, but they could not find it.

**7** When Jeremiah learned of it, he rebuked them and declared: "The place shall be unknown until God gathers his people together again and shows his mercy.

**8** And then the LORD will disclose these things, and the glory of the LORD and the cloud will appear, as they were shown in the case of Moses, and as Solomon asked that the place might be greatly sanctified."

**9** It was also made clear that he, being possessed of wisdom, offered a sacrifice of dedication and of the completion of the temple.

**10** Just as Moses prayed to the LORD and fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifices, so also Solomon prayed, and the fire came down and consumed the whole burnt offerings.

**11** And Moses said, "Because the sin offering was not eaten, it was consumed."

**12** In the same way Solomon also kept the eight days.

**13** The same things were also reported in the records and the memoirs of Nehemiah, and how he, founding a library, gathered together the books about the kings and the prophets, and the books of David, and letters of kings about votive offerings.

**14** In the same way Judas also gathered together all the books that had been scattered on account of the war that had come upon us, and they are in our possession.

**15** If therefore you have need of them, send people to take them to you.

**16** Since, therefore, we are about to celebrate the purification, we write to you. You will do well, therefore, if you celebrate these days.

**17** It is God who has saved all his people and has given to all the heritage and the kingdom and the priesthood and the sanctification,

**18** as he promised through the law — for we hope in God that he will speedily have mercy upon us and will gather us from everywhere under heaven to the holy place, for he has rescued us from great evils and has purified the place.

**19** Now the account of Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, and the purification of the great temple, and the dedication of the altar,

**20** and further the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,

**21** and the appearances from heaven to those who were zealous for Judaism, so that though they were few, they plundered the whole land and put to flight the barbarian hordes,

**22** and recovered the temple celebrated throughout all the world and freed the city and restored the laws that were about to be abolished, seeing that the LORD with all his clemency became gracious toward them —

**23** all these things, I say, which have been set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five volumes, we shall attempt to condense into a single book.

**24** For considering the flood of numbers and the difficulty there is for those who wish to enter into the narratives of the history because of the mass of material,

**25** we have aimed to please those who wish to read, to make it easy for those who are inclined to memorize, and to profit all readers.

**26** For us, who have undertaken the toil of abbreviating, it is not an easy thing but a matter of sweat and late nights,

**27** just as it is not easy for one who prepares a banquet and seeks to benefit others. Nevertheless, to secure the gratitude of many we will gladly endure the uncomfortable toil,

**28** leaving the exact treatment of every particular to the historian, and striving to follow the rules of an epitome.

**29** For just as the architect of a new house must be concerned with the whole structure, while the one who undertakes the decorating and painting seeks only what is suitable for ornamentation, so I consider it to be with us.

**30** To enter into questions and to examine them on all sides and to be curious about details belongs to the author of a history;

**31** but the one who makes an epitome should be permitted to strive for brevity of expression and to forego an exhaustive treatment.

**32** Let this then be the starting point of our narrative; we have said this much by way of preface, for it is foolish to write at great length before the history and then to abridge the history itself.
